rationale: Frontier saturated: best observed latency 29740ms (R4) and best observed quality 0.9703 (R4) each fall ~1000ms / ~0.0034 short of the 2000ms / 0.03 epsilon bars, and both occurred on single-mutation runs that were already reverted. The combination that would clear a gate (R2's compact-JSON on identity.md + R4's summary brevity on section_summary.md) requires two mutations and so cannot be expressed in one action. Every single-mutation re-approach either (a) replays a reverted mechanism and triggers no_repeat_failed_mutations (compact JSON in identity/output_schema; summary-brevity in section_summary; shorter citations in citations.md; citation-count caps per R10), or (b) layers extra directives on top of R4 (R5 pattern) which collapsed summary_quality 0.941→0.841 and json_valid 1.0→0.95, or (c) touches fragile surfaces (output_schema.md edits per R6/R9: -0.047; deleting exclusions.md re-admits padding; sampling perturbations are noise gambling per R6/R7 dismissal). R10 just confirmed the pattern — a non-repeat citation mutation regressed -0.030, hitting the quality floor. Across the lever space, P(gate-clear) × upside < P(regress > 0.03) × downside. Noop preserves the on-frontier R1-kept state (latency 30760, quality 0.9437) rather than burning the round on a mutation with negative expected value. Two prior noops (R6, R7) reached the same conclusion from the same frontier; R10's revert since then has only reinforced the saturation diagnosis.
